open_threads:
1. TWO RECORDS IS NOT A RATE. The ticket's horizon stays open on purpose: does a refusal repeat often enough to need damping the way the trouble lane damps (first raise notifies, later raises increment a count)? One real refusal exists. Notably it argues for the ACTOR-and-code side rather than the boat — a stale fingerprint clears the moment the proof is re-run, exactly the 'refused once then moving' case a naive [X] flag would pin forever.

2. THE TWO VOYAGE MARKERS DID NOT GRAFT, deliberately. [R] requested presumes a DWELL state a synchronous gate has none of — it waits on a design question nobody has asked (should clearance ever be asynchronous?), not on data. [X] refused has its fact and needs a 'still refused since the last journaled crossing' predicate. Both now say so at their own GROW_AGAINST_NEED entries in cairn/devices/harbor_master/voyage.py.

3. A HOLLOW-SCAN LESSON WORTH KEEPING. Criterion 5's instrument was a whole-file grep for 'does not exist yet' and it fired RED after the build — correctly. The cause was a blanket sentence covering a set that had stopped being uniform, so the two markers whose fact this voyage BUILT were still described by a sentence asserting absence. A per-item phrasing fixed it. Same family as the leak-scan coin-toss-red pattern.
